intervention_label: Niraparib comparative pharmacokinetics and efficacy in BRCA-wild-type ovarian PDX
model_system: BRCA-wild-type ovarian cancer PDX (OVC134) in female BALB/c nude mice; >30 ovarian PDX/CDX panel spanning HRD-positive and HRD-negative
n_units: single PDX efficacy arm plus >30-model panel; group sizes per arm not detailed in abstract
dose_and_schedule: niraparib 50 mg/kg PO QD (reduced to 40 mg/kg for weight loss); olaparib 67 mg/kg PO BID (reduced to 60 mg/kg)
mechanism: Niraparib partitions into tumor at 3.3x plasma concentration versus 0.6x for olaparib, giving roughly 16-fold higher dose-normalized tumor exposure. The extra drug in the tumor compartment lets niraparib trap PARP and kill cells that retain functional BRCA, where olaparib fails to reach a cytotoxic threshold.
key_finding: In the BRCA-wild-type OVC134 model niraparib cut tumor growth by 58% while olaparib barely moved it. Across the >30-model ovarian panel, regressions appeared in BRCA-mutant and HRD-positive BRCA-wild-type tumors, with some growth inhibition even in Myriad-defined HRD-negative models.
caveats: Subcutaneous PDX, not orthotopic. Directly on point for this BRCA-wild-type, genomically-unstable tumor: it is the preclinical pharmacology argument for niraparib (PRIMA, all-comers) over BRCA-gated olaparib here.

intervention_label: Differential PARP-trapping potency across PARP inhibitors
model_system: DT40 isogenic chicken B-cell panel and human cancer cell lines with defined DNA-repair backgrounds; cell-free PARP-DNA retention assays
control_arm: PARP-null and repair-proficient isogenic lines; veliparib/olaparib comparators
dose_and_schedule: in vitro exposure across nM-uM range
mechanism: PARP inhibitors differ in how strongly they trap PARP-DNA complexes, and trapping (not just catalytic inhibition) drives cytotoxicity. Niraparib and olaparib are far stronger trappers than veliparib, with trapping potency tracking cell kill more closely than enzymatic IC50.
key_finding: Niraparib ranked among the most potent PARP-trapping agents tested, well above veliparib. The trapping-versus-catalytic distinction explains why a strong trapper can damage genomically unstable, BRCA-proficient cells that survive a weak catalytic-only inhibitor.
caveats: Mechanistic cell-line work, not an ovarian in-vivo efficacy study. Foundational reference for why niraparib's trapping potency matters in a BRCA-wild-type setting; the later DT40 follow-up (Murai 2014) refines the ranking.

intervention_label: Cediranib induces a homologous-recombination defect that sensitizes BRCA-wild-type tumors to olaparib
model_system: BRCA-wild-type ovarian lines (IGROV1, SKOV3, PEO14) plus BRCA2-mutant PEO1/PEO4 and breast lines; IGROV1 and hypoxia-reporter xenografts in nu/nu mice
n_units: multi-line panel; xenograft arms (group sizes per arm not specified in text)
dose_and_schedule: cediranib 3-18 mg/kg in vivo (0.25-32 uM in vitro); olaparib 50 mg/kg in vivo
mechanism: Cediranib drives down BRCA1, BRCA2, and RAD51 through two routes: VEGFR2-mediated tumor hypoxia, and a hypoxia-independent PDGFR-blockade pathway that activates PP2A and E2F4/p130 transcriptional repression. The result is a contextual, drug-induced HR defect in cells that are genetically HR-proficient.
key_finding: Cediranib produced an HR-deficient state in BRCA-wild-type ovarian cells and sensitized them to olaparib both in culture and in xenografts. This is the mechanistic basis for combining a VEGFR inhibitor with a PARP inhibitor in BRCA-proficient HGSC, the exact genetic context of this tumor.
caveats: Cediranib is the tool VEGFR-TKI here, not the patient's bevacizumab; the induced-HRD concept transfers to anti-angiogenic plus PARP strategy but the specific agent differs. Subcutaneous and reporter xenografts rather than orthotopic peritoneal disease.

intervention_label: Triapine plus olaparib plus cediranib in BRCA-wild-type, PARP-inhibitor-resistant ovarian cancer
model_system: BRCA-wild-type, PARP-inhibitor-resistant EOC: SKOV3 and OVCAR3 subcutaneous in nude mice; PEO4ip intraperitoneal in SCID-Beige mice
n_units: per-arm group sizes not stated in abstract; survival cohorts
control_arm: vehicle and lower-order single/double agent arms
dose_and_schedule: triapine 10 mg/kg/day, olaparib 50 mg/kg/day, cediranib 0.75 mg/kg/day
mechanism: Triapine inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and adds replication stress; cediranib suppresses HR via hypoxia and PDGFR blockade; olaparib traps PARP. Stacking the three converges on the same DNA-repair vulnerability in tumors that are genetically HR-proficient and have escaped single-agent PARP inhibition.
key_finding: In the intraperitoneal PEO4ip model the triple combination extended median survival to 89 days versus 62 in controls and beat every lower-order arm. Supports layering anti-angiogenic and replication-stress agents onto a PARP inhibitor in BRCA-wild-type, PARP-resistant disease.
caveats: Triapine is not on this patient's option list, so the directly transferable insight is the cediranib-plus-olaparib backbone in BRCA-wild-type disease. PEO4ip carries a reverted BRCA2, a resistance model rather than a naive maintenance setting.

intervention_label: VEGF immunoneutralization controls ovarian tumor growth and ascites
model_system: Human SKOV-3 ovarian carcinoma, subcutaneous and intraperitoneal, in immunodeficient mice; treated with anti-VEGF antibody A4.6.1 (the murine antecedent of bevacizumab)
n_units: xenograft cohorts (group sizes per arm not specified in abstract)
dose_and_schedule: A4.6.1 anti-VEGF antibody after 7-10 day engraftment
mechanism: VEGF supports ovarian tumor growth by driving neovascularization and raises vascular permeability to produce malignant ascites. Blocking VEGF starves the angiogenic supply and shuts down the permeability that fills the peritoneal cavity.
key_finding: A4.6.1 significantly slowed subcutaneous SKOV-3 growth, partly slowed intraperitoneal growth, and abolished ascites formation; tumor regrew once antibody was withdrawn. This is the founding preclinical rationale for the VEGF-maintenance axis the patient is already on with bevacizumab.
caveats: A4.6.1 is the precursor antibody clone, not clinical bevacizumab, and growth resumed off-therapy, mirroring the maintenance-not-cure clinical pattern. Older study; the ascites-control finding remains the cleanest mechanistic anchor for anti-VEGF here.

intervention_label: Bevacizumab maintenance after chemotherapy in ovarian carcinoma xenografts
model_system: Human epithelial ovarian carcinoma xenografts (including HOC22) in mice; chemotherapy plus bevacizumab in concurrent, maintenance, and sequential schedules
n_units: multiple xenograft arms (per-arm group sizes not stated in abstract)
dose_and_schedule: cisplatin plus paclitaxel induction; bevacizumab concurrent, as maintenance after induction, or started after chemotherapy
mechanism: Adding bevacizumab to platinum-taxane chemotherapy suppresses VEGF-driven angiogenesis during and after cytotoxic treatment. Continuing it as maintenance keeps the residual tumor vasculature suppressed once chemotherapy stops.
key_finding: Bevacizumab with cisplatin and paclitaxel delayed progression, and continuing it as maintenance after chemotherapy gave the longest survival, with complete responses in the HOC22 model. Preclinical mirror of the GOG-218/ICON7 maintenance schedule this patient is on.
caveats: PMID not independently confirmed in this run; DOI verified (10.1038/bjc.2012.261). Schedule-comparison xenograft work; the maintenance arm is the load-bearing result for the patient's current bevacizumab continuation.

intervention_label: Aromatase inhibition in ER-alpha-positive ovarian cancer xenografts
model_system: Ovariectomized nude mice with peritoneal carcinomatosis: OVCAR-3 (strong ER-alpha) versus DISS (weak ER-alpha)
n_units: survival cohorts per line (sizes not stated in abstract)
mechanism: Aromatase inhibition lowers local estrogen and blunts ER-alpha signaling in ER-positive ovarian tumors. Downstream it reduces VEGF and tumor microvessel density, tying the endocrine effect to an anti-angiogenic, anti-ascites readout.
key_finding: Letrozole prolonged survival in the strongly ER-alpha-positive OVCAR-3 model but did nothing in the weakly positive DISS model, and lowered tumor VEGF and microvessel density. The ER-magnitude dependence fits this patient's ~80% ER-positive but PR-negative profile as a real-but-modest endocrine signal.
caveats: Benefit tracked ER-alpha intensity, and this tumor is ER-positive but PR-negative, predicting a tempered response. No HGSC-specific orthotopic arm; OVCAR-3 is a serous-type line.

intervention_label: IL-12 plasmid lipopolymer (GEN-1 / EGEN-001) intraperitoneal immunogene therapy: ID8 preclinical basis
model_system: Murine ID8 intraperitoneal ovarian tumor model dosed with mouse IL-12 plasmid formulated in PEG-PEI-cholesterol lipopolymer (pmIL-12/PPC); plus first-in-human phase I
n_units: tumor-bearing mouse cohorts plus 13-patient phase I
dose_and_schedule: pmIL-12/PPC ~100 ug/treatment IP, dosing from ~day 18 post-implant, with or without carboplatin/paclitaxel
mechanism: Local intraperitoneal delivery of an IL-12-encoding plasmid produces sustained, compartment-restricted IL-12 and IFN-gamma rather than a short systemic protein bolus. That shifts the peritoneal immune microenvironment toward a Th1 program and lowers ascitic VEGF.
key_finding: In ID8 mice, pmIL-12/PPC raised peritoneal IL-12 and IFN-gamma, drove a Th1 gene-expression shift, dropped ascitic VEGF, and improved survival alone and with chemotherapy. Mechanistic foundation for the GEN-1/IMNN-001 program this patient received, working through the TME rather than the foreclosed MSI/TMB checkpoint axis.
caveats: The ID8 preclinical package is reported alongside the phase I in this and companion Imunon/EGEN sources rather than as a single standalone mouse paper; treat as the preclinical-plus-early-clinical anchor. Syngeneic ID8 immunogenicity may exceed human HGSC, and MSS/TMB-low status argues against single-agent checkpoint blockade, not against this IL-12 route.

intervention_label: PI3K inhibition (BKM120) plus olaparib in PIK3CA-altered ovarian cancer
model_system: PIK3CA-altered ovarian lines (SKOV3, HEYA8, IGROV1, EFO27); intraperitoneal SKOV3-luciferase dissemination xenograft in NOD/SCID mice
n_units: multi-line panel; IP xenograft cohort (per-arm sizes not stated in abstract)
dose_and_schedule: BKM120 (buparlisib) plus olaparib, single-agent and combination per protocol
mechanism: Pan-class-I PI3K inhibition with BKM120 lowers BRCA1/2 expression in responsive PIK3CA-altered ovarian cells, manufacturing a homologous-recombination defect. That induced HRD then makes otherwise HR-proficient cells vulnerable to PARP trapping.
key_finding: BKM120 plus olaparib was synergistic, raising DNA damage and apoptosis and shrinking tumor burden in the intraperitoneal model; cells that dropped BRCA1/2 most on PI3K inhibition responded best. Investigational rationale connecting the patient's PIK3CA amplification to the PARP/HRD axis, distinct from the foreclosed BRCA-mutation route.
caveats: Models carry PIK3CA point mutations; the patient has PIK3CA amplification, so the dependency may differ in degree. Strictly investigational, with no approved PI3K-directed therapy in HGSC; surfaced as a mechanism-level link, not a near-term option.

exclusion_reason: PI3Kalpha inhibitor (BYL-719/alpelisib) plus cisplatin synergy was shown in PIK3CA-mutant ovarian cells in vitro only, with no in-vivo arm, and keys on PIK3CA hotspot mutation rather than the patient's amplification. The PI3K/HRD axis is already covered by the Wang 2016 in-vivo row; logged for audit trail.
intervention_label: PI3Kalpha inhibitor BYL-719 plus cisplatin in PIK3CA-mutant ovarian cells

exclusion_reason: No primary preclinical study ties a MAP2K4 (MKK4) deletion to a tractable, validated drug target in ovarian cancer; the literature treats MAP2K4 loss as a poorly-characterized JNK/p38-pathway event with no matched agent. Nothing meets the bar for an included mechanism row, so this records the negative search result rather than logging trial-list baskets as preclinical evidence.
intervention_label: MAP2K4 (MKK4) deletion as a drug target in ovarian cancer

model_system: HER2-positive breast and gastric cell lines plus breast PDX models, including low-HER2 and T-DM1-refractory PDX, in mice
n_units: multi-line panel plus several PDX arms; per-arm group sizes not stated in the abstract
dose_and_schedule: DS-8201a IV; tumor regression at doses above 1 mg/kg in gastric models
mechanism: DS-8201a carries about 8 exatecan-derivative topoisomerase I payloads per antibody against T-DM1's roughly 3.5, and the freed DXd crosses cell membranes. The heavier payload load plus a diffusible toxin reaches tumor cells that take up little HER2.
key_finding: Growth inhibition tracked HER2 level but did not need high expression: DS-8201a regressed breast PDX models with low HER2 and tumors that had stopped responding to T-DM1. Chk1 and gamma-H2AX phosphorylation confirmed the topoisomerase I DNA-damage route.
caveats: Breast and gastric models, no ovarian arm. The low-HER2 activity is the load-bearing point for an IHC 1+ tumor, but the proof here sits in a different tissue.

intervention_label: T-DXd (DS-8201a) bystander killing in HER2-heterogeneous tumors
model_system: Coculture of HER2-positive KPL-4 with HER2-negative MDA-MB-468; mixed NCI-N87 (HER2+) and luciferase-tagged MDA-MB-468 (HER2-) xenografts in nude mice, with a separate opposite-flank HER2-negative tumor
n_units: in-vitro cocultures plus mixed-population and dual-flank xenograft cohorts; group sizes not stated in the abstract
control_arm: T-DM1; opposite-flank HER2-negative tumor as a spatial control
mechanism: DXd freed inside a HER2-positive cell is membrane-permeable, so it passes into neighboring cells whatever their HER2 level. T-DM1's charged Lys-SMCC-DM1 payload stays trapped and produces no such spillover.
key_finding: In mixed cultures and co-implanted xenografts DS-8201a killed the HER2-negative population, but it left HER2-negative tumors growing on the opposite flank untouched. Bystander reach is local and needs HER2-positive cells nearby.
caveats: Breast and gastric lines, not ovarian. An IHC 1+ tumor carries sparse HER2-positive cells, so how far the local bystander effect extends at that antigen density is the open question this study cannot answer.

intervention_label: T-DXd (DS-8201a) in ovarian and uterine carcinosarcoma
model_system: 12 primary carcinosarcoma cell lines (8 uterine, 4 ovarian) across HER2/neu 3+/1+/0; in vivo SARARK-9 HER2 3+ uterine flank xenograft in mice
n_units: 12 primary lines (3 used in vitro); n=5 mice/arm in vivo (n=4 vehicle, days 4-11)
control_arm: isotype-control ADC MAAA-9199 (4 mg/kg) and PBS vehicle
dose_and_schedule: DS-8201a 4 mg/kg, single retro-orbital IV injection
mechanism: Same DXd topoisomerase I payload and membrane-permeable bystander spillover, tested in gynecologic carcinosarcoma. Cytotoxicity scaled with HER2/neu, and the freed payload reached adjacent HER2-null cells in coculture.
key_finding: In HER2 3+ ovarian and uterine lines DS-8201a IC50 ran about 0.03 uM against roughly 9 uM for the isotype control, with no separation in the HER2-0 line. Coculture gave 52% killing of HER2-0 cells next to 3+ cells, and the 3+ xenograft regressed with 60% of mice disease-free at day 52.
caveats: The only ovarian in-vivo T-DXd data in this dossier, but the tissue is carcinosarcoma rather than high-grade serous and the xenograft used a HER2 3+ line. In-vitro potency was quantified at 3+ and 0, not at the patient's 1+ tier, so activity at IHC 1+ rests on the bystander route rather than direct proof.

intervention_label: Disitamab vedotin (RC48) preclinical antitumor activity, monotherapy and with tucatinib
model_system: Panel of HER2-expressing cancer cell lines and xenografts; specific lines and HER2 tiers not itemized in the meeting abstract
n_units: cell-line and xenograft panel; sizes not detailed in the abstract
control_arm: monotherapy versus tucatinib combination; comparator ADC not detailed
mechanism: Disitamab vedotin releases MMAE after HER2 binding and internalization; MMAE is membrane-permeable and spills into neighboring cells whatever their HER2 level. The sponsor also credits immunogenic cell death and Fc-mediated ADCC.
key_finding: RC48 controlled HER2-expressing tumors as monotherapy and gained further depth combined with tucatinib, with the MMAE bystander effect offered as the route to activity in HER2-low or heterogeneous tumors. Per-model HER2-low potency was not broken out.
caveats: Sponsor conference abstract with no per-model HER2-low numbers and no ovarian model. It carries the MMAE bystander rationale, not a quantified low-expression result; the matching urothelial and HER2-low breast efficacy reads sit in the clinical rows.

exclusion_reason: Reviewed while hunting for the MMAE bystander basis, but this is a different molecule: a biparatopic HER2 ADC (MEDI4276) carrying a tubulysin microtubule inhibitor, not disitamab vedotin's MMAE conjugate. It targets T-DM1-refractory HER2-positive disease rather than the HER2-low tier, so both payload and population diverge from the intervention.

intervention_label: Trastuzumab duocarmazine (SYD985) preclinical profile in low-HER2 breast cancer
model_system: Breast cancer cell lines and PDX models spanning HER2 3+, 2+, and 1+; HER2-0 cells mixed with 3+/2+/1+ cells for bystander assays
n_units: low- and high-HER2 cell lines plus breast PDX models; per-arm sizes not stated in the abstract
mechanism: SYD985 carries a duocarmycin (vc-seco-DUBA) on a cathepsin-B-cleavable linker; the freed seco-DUBA is membrane-permeable and stays active across tumor-relevant pH, so it kills HER2-low cells directly and reaches HER2-negative neighbors.
key_finding: In low-HER2 lines SYD985 was 3- to 50-fold more potent than T-DM1, and it regressed HER2 1+, 2+, and 3+ breast PDX models where T-DM1 worked only at 3+. HER2-0 cells were killed when mixed with 1+, 2+, or 3+ cells.
caveats: Breast cell lines and PDX, no ovarian model. The clinical program is shelved after Byondis halted development on the FDA complete response letter, so this stands as HER2-low mechanism evidence rather than backing for a live option.
